territorial_scope.description: Federal statute amending Title 17 of the United States Code; subpoenas are issued by U.S. district court clerks to developers.

evidence.quote: Chapter 5 of title 17, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following:

summary.short: Creates a 17 U.S.C. § 514 process letting copyright owners request a clerk-issued subpoena compelling generative AI developers to disclose copies or records identifying copyrighted works used to train their models. Developers must comply expeditiously; non-compliance creates a rebuttable presumption of copying; bad-faith requests may be sanctioned. Effective on enactment.
summary.long: As introduced, the bill adds § 514 to Chapter 5 of title 17, United States Code. The legal or beneficial owner of an exclusive copyright right, or an authorized person, may file with a U.S. district court clerk a proposed subpoena and a sworn declaration stating a subjective good-faith belief that a developer used the owner's works to train a generative AI model. If the filing is in proper form, the clerk issues the subpoena. A developer receiving it must expeditiously disclose copies of, or records sufficient to identify with certainty, the training material. Requests are limited to the requester's own works. Recipients of disclosed material may not disclose it to others without authorization. Issuance, service and enforcement follow the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure, and noncompliance creates a rebuttable presumption that the developer made copies of the work. Courts may impose Rule 11(c)-style sanctions for bad-faith requests on motion of the recipient. The section takes effect on enactment.

relations.note: Adds new section 514 at the end of chapter 5 (subpoena for copies or records relating to artificial intelligence models), per Sec. 2(a).

notes: Introduced bill text (S.2455, 119th Congress); the document contains no legislative history or later versions. Target instruments for title 17 and the Federal Rules are not in the registry as given, so target_instrument_id is blank. Internal points: proposed 514(d) says the subpoena 'shall authorize and order' disclosure while 514(e) has the clerk issue it on a proper form and declaration; 514(i) creates a rebuttable presumption from non-compliance, and 514(h) leaves remedies for noncompliance to the Federal Rules 'to the greatest extent practicable'. Section 2(k) makes the new section effective on enactment.

thresholds.note: No numeric cutoff changes legal treatment in the operative provisions of S.2455 (Sec. 2, new 17 U.S.C. § 514). The only numbers are citations (15 U.S.C. 9401, title 17, Rule 11) and section numbers. The 'good faith belief' and 'bad faith' standards are not numeric, and procedural timing is not coded as thresholds.
